fact: Delhi has 170 of India's 3,685 centrally protected monuments, 4.6% of them, on 0.05% of India's land.
compare: 115 per 1,000 sq km against 1.1 for India and 14 in Puducherry, the next densest; Delhi area 1,483 sq km (Census 2011)
source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
stays_true: Changes by a few when the Government notifies or de-notifies a site (3 Delhi sites were removed in 2024-25); no fixed schedule, the next Parliament answer or ASI list shows it. Area is Census 2011 (fixed).
lead: 8.0x the density of Puducherry
size_effect: Opposite of a size effect: Delhi is among the smallest territories (Census 2011 area 1,483 sq km); its share of monuments is about 100 times its share of land (102x).
caution: The count moves slightly: ASI's list PDF (April 2025) has Delhi 172 of 3,698, Parliament (1 Dec 2025) has 170 of 3,685 after delistings, ASI's web page says 3,679 in total. Use the December 2025 figures; the density lead over Puducherry is huge on every version. Monuments are counted without grouping by kind.

fact: Tamil Nadu has 412 of India's 3,685 centrally protected monuments, 11% of them, on 4% of India's land.
compare: Share of monuments 11.2% against 4.0% of area and 6.0% of people (Census 2011); 2.8x its area share
source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
stays_true: Changes by a few when a site is notified or de-notified (Tamil Nadu was 412 in both the April 2025 ASI list and the December 2025 Parliament answer); no fixed schedule.
lead: Third among States/UTs (Uttar Pradesh 735, Karnataka 506); no first-place claim
size_effect: Share of monuments is 2.8x its area share and 1.9x its population share, so size does not explain it.
caution: Centrally protected only; state-protected monuments are separate and not in this table.

fact: Karnataka has 506 centrally protected monuments, more than any State but Uttar Pradesh, 13.7% of India's 3,685.
compare: 13.7% of India's monuments against 5.0% of its people and 5.8% of its land (Census 2011); 2.7x its population share
source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
stays_true: Changes by a few when a site is notified or de-notified (Karnataka was 506 in both the April 2025 ASI list and the December 2025 answer); Goa 21 likewise; no fixed schedule.
lead: 94 ahead of Tamil Nadu (23% more); Uttar Pradesh is first with 735 (743 in the April 2025 list)
size_effect: Karnataka is 5.0% of India's people, so its 13.7% share is 2.7x its population share. ASI keeps three circles here (Bangalore, Dharwad, Hampi).
caution: Centrally protected only. Second place needs the 3% / 1 point rule vs Tamil Nadu (met).

fact: Goa, India's smallest State by area, has 21 centrally protected monuments: 5.7 per 1,000 sq km against 1.1 for India.
measure: Centrally protected monuments and sites per 1,000 sq km
compare: India 1.12 per 1,000 sq km; Goa is 5.1x the national density; Goa area 3,702 sq km (Census 2011)
source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 84, 1 Dec 2025, Annexure-I (ASI figures); cross-checked with ASI list PDF CPM_List.pdf (created 8 Apr 2025)
stays_true: Changes by a few when a site is notified or de-notified (Karnataka was 506 in both the April 2025 ASI list and the December 2025 answer); Goa 21 likewise; no fixed schedule.
lead: Third densest after Delhi and Puducherry (Goa 5.7; Puducherry 14.3; Delhi 115); no first claim
size_effect: A density, so the small area is the point: the count (21) is itself small.
caution: Same 21 in the April 2025 ASI list. Smallest State by area: Census 2011 areas Goa 3,702 sq km, Sikkim 7,096; UTs are smaller. Density uses Census 2011 area. Do not say 'densest'.

fact: Maharashtra has 7 of India's 45 UNESCO World Heritage properties, the most of any State; Tamil Nadu has 5.
measure: UNESCO World Heritage properties (a shared property counted once under each State)
compare: Tamil Nadu 5; Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, Rajasthan 4 each; Maharashtra is 9.3% of India's people
column: World Heritage properties (counted under each State/UT named)
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I
stays_true: Changes when UNESCO's World Heritage Committee inscribes a new property at its yearly session; the next session's decisions are the next change.
lead: 2 ahead (40% more) than Tamil Nadu; same lead on the 44-property list of Aug 2025
size_effect: Maharashtra holds 15.6% of properties with 9.3% of people (1.7x): modest, so rank is the story, not size.
caution: Six of the seven are cultural plus the shared natural Western Ghats; the Maratha Military Landscapes (2025) and Western Ghats (2012) are shared with Tamil Nadu. Counting shared properties once under each State is stated in the table.

fact: Delhi's 1,483 sq km hold 3 of India's 45 World Heritage properties: Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb and Qutb Minar.
compare: 6.7% of India's properties on 0.05% of its land; 148x its area share
column: World Heritage properties (counted under each State/UT named)
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I
stays_true: Delhi's three were inscribed in 1993 and 2007; changes only if UNESCO inscribes another Delhi property.
lead: Not a rank claim
size_effect: Opposite of a size effect: area 1,483 sq km (Census 2011).
caution: Property names follow UNESCO; Humayun's Tomb and Qutb Minar are inscribed as 'Delhi' sites. State from the Ministry's Lok Sabha answer.

fact: Assam holds 2 of India's 7 natural World Heritage sites, Kaziranga and Manas, on 2.4% of India's land.
compare: 29% of India's natural properties; Assam is 2.4% of area and 2.6% of people; every other State holds at most 1
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I
stays_true: Natural inscriptions are rare (latest 2014 Great Himalayan National Park, 2016 Khangchendzonga as mixed); changes only if UNESCO inscribes another natural property.
lead: 2 against a maximum of 1 for any other State (Western Ghats is one property shared by four States)
size_effect: Assam is 2.4% of India's land, and the share of natural properties is 12x that.
caution: Khangchendzonga (Sikkim) is listed as mixed, so is not counted as natural here. Assam's third property, Moidams (2024), is cultural.

fact: India's only mixed natural and cultural World Heritage property, Khangchendzonga National Park, is in Sikkim, a State of 7,096 sq km.
measure: Mixed (natural and cultural) World Heritage properties
compare: 1 of India's 45 properties; Sikkim is 0.22% of India's land and 0.05% of its people (Census 2011)
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I
stays_true: Stays true until UNESCO inscribes another mixed property in India (none since 2016).
lead: Only one in India (1 of 1)
size_effect: Small State holding the only property of its kind; no size effect.
caution: 'Mixed' is UNESCO's category for sites meeting both natural and cultural criteria. Inscribed 2016.

fact: India's three newest World Heritage inscriptions: Moidams, Assam (2024); Maratha Military Landscapes (2025); Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh (2026).
measure: Newest UNESCO World Heritage inscriptions in India
compare: UNESCO has 45 properties in India, 37 cultural; the three newest are all cultural
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India page (Internet Archive capture 12 Oct 2026) and data.unesco.org dataset whc001; State from Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3591 of 11 Aug 2025, Annexure-I
stays_true: Overtaken when the World Heritage Committee inscribes the next property at its next yearly session; the fact then becomes 'the second-newest'.
lead: Not a rank claim
size_effect: Chronology, not size.
caution: Date-sensitive by nature (ages with the next session) but true as stated. The official name of the 2026 property is 'Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath'; it is a monument, not grouped by faith. The 2026 inscription's State comes from the Ministry's tentative list entry; UNESCO's page gives no State.

fact: Maharashtra has 39 registered agricultural GIs, such as Nashik Grapes and Alphonso mango, 14 more than any other State.
measure: Registered Geographical Indications of kind Agricultural
compare: Next: Tamil Nadu and Kerala with 25 each; 71% of Maharashtra's 55 GIs are agricultural against 33% across India
source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025
stays_true: The register grows every year (125 rows in April 2025 to March 2026), so a State can be overtaken; true as stated for 31 March 2026. Next edition: the Registry's next year-wise register.
lead: 14 ahead (56% more) than the next State; on the 31 Dec 2025 list (shared GIs counted under each State) it was 38 against 25 for Tamil Nadu, with Karnataka 24
size_effect: Maharashtra is 9.3% of India's people but holds a 15% share of agricultural GIs and a 71% share within its own GIs; the lead over equally large States is wide.
caution: Kind is the register's 'Goods' column: 'Agriculture' and 'Agricultural' merged; 'Food Stuff' is a separate kind. 39 counts Nagpur Orange once under Maharashtra and once under Madhya Pradesh (shared). Names in the example are from the register.

fact: India's first three registered GIs, in 2004-05, were Darjeeling Tea (West Bengal), Pochampalli Ikat (Telangana) and Chanderi Sarees (Madhya Pradesh).
measure: First Geographical Indications registered in India (April 2004 to March 2005)
compare: By 31 March 2026 the register had 820 rows (780 Indian, 40 foreign)
column: GIs registered (counted under each State/UT named)
source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025
as_on: 31 March 2026 (register); first-year entries are fixed history
stays_true: The first-year rows are history and cannot change.
lead: Not a rank claim
size_effect: History, not size.
caution: Darjeeling Tea is entered twice (word and logo, serials 1 and 2) but is one GI. The register lists Pochampalli Ikat under Telangana as printed.

fact: Basmati is one registered GI shared by seven States and UTs: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.
measure: States/UTs named in a single GI
compare: Every other multi-State GI in the register names two or three States (17 shared GIs in all)
source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025
stays_true: A registered GI's named States change only by amendment; Basmati has named these for years.
lead: 7 against 3 for the next widest (Malabar Pepper, Phulkari, Warli)
size_effect: Not a size matter.
caution: In the register Basmati's states appear as 'Punjab / Haryana / Himachal Pradesh / Delhi / Uttarkhand / Uttar Pradesh / Jammu & Kashmir'; Uttar Pradesh's inclusion is as printed. Lead state field is not a lead; it is one of seven.

fact: Uttarakhand has 29 registered GIs, 3.7% of India's, with 0.8% of its people.
compare: 4.5x its population share (Census 2011); 17 of 29 are agricultural
column: GIs registered (counted under each State/UT named)
source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025
stays_true: The register grows yearly; Uttarakhand's count was also 29 on the 31 Dec 2025 list. Next edition: next year-wise register.
lead: No rank claim (Uttarakhand is 10th by count)
size_effect: Share of GIs is 4.5x its population share; small-State effect, not a size effect.
caution: Share of India = 29 / 780 Indian GI entries; the shared GI is counted under each State. Population share is Census 2011 (10,086,292).

fact: Ladakh has 11 registered GIs, 9 of them handicrafts, and 7 of the 11 were registered between April 2025 and March 2026.
compare: On 31 Dec 2025 Ladakh had 4; projected population about 0.30 million (1 March 2026)
source: GI Registry (DPIIT), Year-wise GI Application Register as on 31 March 2026 (ipindia.gov.in, file created 27 May 2026); previous edition: State-wise Registered GI list as on 31 Dec 2025
stays_true: Date-bound: 11 as of 31 March 2026; further registrations will raise it. Next edition: next year-wise register.
lead: No rank claim
size_effect: A small-population UT; no size effect.
caution: Weak as evergreen: the count rose from 4 to 11 in one quarter. Use only as 'as of March 2026'. The register prints Ladakh Likir Pottery under Assam, so Ladakh could be 12.

fact: Manipur has 212,481 handloom weavers: about one for every 15 people, 34 times India's rate, in the 2019-20 handloom census.
compare: India 2.0 per 1,000; next Arunachal Pradesh 51.1, then Assam 31.9; Manipur has 7.9% of India's weavers and 0.23% of its people
source: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20, Annexure II Tables 1-2 (handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Statistics/3736.pdf); projected population (Population Projections 2011-2036, MoHFW, July 2020)
stays_true: A census of 2019-20; it changes only when the Fifth Handloom Census is published (no date announced as far as we found).
lead: 33% above Arunachal Pradesh; in the 2009-10 census Manipur also led (adult weavers 200,607 on Census 2011 population 2,855,794 = 70 per 1,000, Assam 45)
size_effect: A rate per person, so population size is removed. A small State leads.
caution: 'Weavers' as defined by the census (not allied workers). Population is the official projection for 1 March 2020, printed as 'projected population'. Assam's raw lead (11 lakh weavers) is already in Short fa06.

fact: Manipur has 204,508 women handloom weavers, more than West Bengal's 175,751, with 3% of West Bengal's people.
compare: West Bengal 175,751; Tamil Nadu 93,448; India 1,914,499; Manipur 10.7% of India's women weavers
source: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20, Annexure II Tables 1-2 (handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Statistics/3736.pdf)
stays_true: A census of 2019-20; changes with the Fifth Handloom Census.
lead: 28,757 ahead (16% more) than West Bengal, third; Assam is first with 1,031,717. In 2009-10 (adult weavers) Manipur 199,111 led West Bengal 148,117
size_effect: Manipur is 0.23% of India's people, so its 10.7% share is 46x its population share.
caution: Second-place claim for Manipur is true on both censuses behind Assam. West Bengal's population is the 1 March 2020 projection.

fact: In the 2019-20 handloom census, 96 of every 100 Manipur weavers are women; Odisha 20, India 72.
measure: Women as a share of handloom weavers
compare: Odisha 20.2%, Karnataka 21.3%, Telangana 22.0%; India 71.6%; Assam 93.2%, Nagaland 94.1%
source: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20, Annexure II Tables 1-2 (handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Statistics/3736.pdf)
stays_true: A census of 2019-20; changes with the Fifth Handloom Census.
lead: No rank claim: Sikkim (96.8% of 632 weavers) is higher than Manipur (96.2%), and Nagaland is within 3% of it
size_effect: A share, not a count.
caution: Do not rank; use as a contrast between regions. 'Weavers' excludes allied workers. In the 2009-10 census Odisha was 15% and Haryana, Delhi, Chhattisgarh lower, so Odisha is not 'lowest' there.

fact: Arunachal Pradesh has 77,600 handloom weavers, 2.9% of India's, with 0.11% of its people.
compare: 51.1 per 1,000 people against India 2.0 (projected 1 March 2020); 85% of them women
source: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20, Annexure II Tables 1-2 (handlooms.nic.in/assets/img/Statistics/3736.pdf)
stays_true: A census of 2019-20; changes with the Fifth Handloom Census.
lead: Second per person after Manipur in 2019-20 (by 60% over Assam); not second in 2009-10, so no rank claim
size_effect: 26x its population share; a small State.
caution: The 2009-10 census counted 25,872 adult weavers here against 77,600 in 2019-20, so the two censuses are probably not comparable; avoid trend claims.

fact: ASI's village-to-village survey reached 1,459 villages in Punjab between 2014-15 and 2023-24, more than in any other State.
measure: Villages surveyed by ASI to find archaeological sites
compare: Next: Karnataka 943, Uttarakhand 907; Punjab is 1.5% of India's land
source: Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 2237, 9 Dec 2024, Annexure
stays_true: A closed ten-year period, true as stated; later years' surveys do not change it. A new ten-year table would only appear if Parliament is asked again.
lead: 516 ahead (55% more) than Karnataka
size_effect: Punjab is 1.5% of India's land, so the lead is not size.
caution: Counts survey effort (villages visited), not monuments found; the answer gives no reason. 26 States/UTs listed; others are not stated as zero.

fact: India has 11 classical languages; five of them, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali, were added on 3 October 2024.
compare: Six before 2024: Tamil 2004, Sanskrit 2005, Telugu and Kannada 2008, Malayalam 2013, Odia 2014
source: Ministry of Culture, 'Status of Classical Language: An Explainer', 4 Oct 2024 (PIB)
stays_true: True as stated until the Union Cabinet adds another language; no schedule exists. Next edition: a new Ministry of Culture notification.
lead: 5 of 11 on one date
size_effect: Not a size matter.
caution: The Ministry does not name a State per language; do not assign States in the script without a source. The Cabinet decision date is 3 Oct 2024; the explainer is dated 4 Oct.

fact: Tamil was the first language declared classical in India, on 12 October 2004; Sanskrit followed on 25 November 2005.
compare: Eleven languages now hold the status
source: Ministry of Culture, 'Status of Classical Language: An Explainer', 4 Oct 2024 (PIB)
stays_true: A past date; cannot change.
lead: First of 11
size_effect: History.
caution: State field is a convenience (Tamil's home State); the Ministry's table names no State. Notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

fact: Telugu and Kannada were declared classical languages on the same day, 31 October 2008.
measure: Classical language declarations on one date
compare: Malayalam followed on 8 August 2013 and Odia on 1 March 2014
source: Ministry of Culture, 'Status of Classical Language: An Explainer', 4 Oct 2024 (PIB)
stays_true: A past date; cannot change.
lead: Not a rank claim
size_effect: History.
caution: State field is a convenience (home State of Kannada; Telugu's are Andhra Pradesh and Telangana); the Ministry's table names no State.
